analysis.headline: USD/KRW drops to 1,339.0 as post-election momentum fades and exporters sell dollars
analysis.summary: USD/KRW declined to around 1,339.0 (ECB ref 1,339.00) as the post-election dollar rally ran out of steam and U.S. Treasury yields stabilized. A rebound in global tech equities and massive dollar sales (nego) by Korean exporters above 1,340 KRW fueled won gains. Trading settled in a 1,336–1,345 KRW range as markets awaited October U.S. inflation data.

analysis.headline: EUR/KRW declines to 1,501.6 as steep won appreciation outweighs steady EUR/USD
analysis.summary: EUR/KRW retreated toward 1,501.6 (ECB ref 1,501.56), testing the 1,500 KRW psychological floor. While EUR/USD held steady near 1.1214 amid stabilizing crude oil prices and cooling U.S. yields, the Korean won appreciated at a significantly faster pace in Seoul. Heavy exporter dollar selling pressured the cross lower within a 1,498–1,506 KRW corridor.

analysis.headline: JPY/KRW falls to 846.5 per 100 JPY as USD/JPY hovers near 158 and won surges
analysis.summary: JPY/KRW slipped to around 8.47 KRW per JPY (~846.5 KRW per 100 JPY, ECB ref 8.465). USD/JPY traded high near 158 on persistent U.S.-Japan yield divergence, though verbal intervention warnings from Tokyo and BOJ rate hike prospects capped yen losses. With the Korean won advancing rapidly on improving tech sentiment, the cross softened into the 844–851 KRW range.

analysis.headline: GBP/KRW slides below 1,800 to 1,797.3 despite support from BoE 4.0% bank rate
analysis.summary: GBP/KRW dropped to around 1,797.3 (ECB ref 1,797.31), breaking below the 1,800 KRW threshold. The Bank of England’s hawkish stance following its rate hike to 4.0% and a steady GBP/USD near 1.34 provided fundamental support. Nonetheless, intense dollar liquidation by Korean exporters sparked a sharp won rally that pushed the cross lower to close between 1,793 and 1,804 KRW.

analysis.headline: CNY/KRW eases to 200.7 as PBOC liquidity supports amidst broader won rally
analysis.summary: CNY/KRW adjusted lower to around 200.7 (ECB ref 200.74) within a 200.0–201.8 KRW range. The PBOC maintained accommodative short-term liquidity injections and steady reference fixings, while expectations for fiscal stimulus from the NPC Standing Committee provided baseline support. However, as USD/KRW tumbled toward 1,339 in Seoul, the cross followed downward to trade between 200.0 and 201.5 KRW.

AUD.headline: AUD slips to 924.4 KRW as won gains overshadow RBA hawkish stance
AUD.brief: The Australian dollar softened to 924.4 KRW as broad Korean won strength offset support from the Reserve Bank of Australia’s hawkish policy and commodity price stability.

CAD.headline: CAD declines to 947.2 KRW pressured by BoC easing and won strength
CAD.brief: The Canadian dollar dropped to 947.2 KRW, weighed down by the Bank of Canada’s monetary easing cycle and oil price consolidation alongside Korean won gains.

CHF.headline: CHF eases to 1,631.6 KRW as risk appetite revives and tech stocks rally
CHF.brief: The Swiss franc receded to 1,631.6 KRW as safe-haven demand diminished amid stabilizing global risk sentiment, a tech equity rebound, and won appreciation.

CNY.headline: CNY eases to 200.7 KRW tracking USD/KRW amid PBOC liquidity support
CNY.brief: The Chinese yuan moved lower to 200.7 KRW, buffered by PBOC liquidity injections and fiscal stimulus expectations but pulled down by the broader drop in USD/KRW.

EUR.headline: EUR retreats to 1,501.6 KRW as won appreciation outpaces EUR/USD
EUR.brief: The euro fell to 1,501.6 KRW as the Korean won appreciated at a faster rate in Seoul, dragging the cross lower toward 1,500 KRW despite EUR/USD holding around 1.1214.

GBP.headline: GBP dips below 1,800 to 1,797.3 KRW as won rally offsets BoE 4.0% rate
GBP.brief: The British pound fell to 1,797.3 KRW as aggressive dollar selling by Korean exporters outweighed support from the Bank of England’s 4.0% policy rate differential.

HKD.headline: HKD eases to 170.7 KRW tracking dollar pullback in Seoul trading
HKD.brief: The Hong Kong dollar eased to 170.7 KRW within its 7.75–7.85 peg band, closely mirroring the decline in USD/KRW as corporate dollar selling dominated Seoul.

JPY.headline: JPY slips to 846.5 KRW per 100 JPY as USD/JPY hovers near 158
JPY.brief: The Japanese yen softened to 846.5 KRW per 100 JPY due to U.S.-Japan yield divergence, though Tokyo intervention warnings and BOJ hike bets cushioned the downside.

KRW.headline: Won strengthens to 1,339.0 KRW on exporter dollar selling and tech exports
KRW.brief: The Korean won rallied to 1,339.0 per dollar, powered by heavy corporate dollar liquidation above 1,340, robust AI semiconductor exports, and improving risk appetite.

USD.headline: USD drops to 1,339.0 KRW on yield easing and corporate exporter selling
USD.brief: The U.S. dollar tumbled to 1,339.0 KRW as post-election momentum waned, Treasury yields cooled, and corporate exporters heavily offloaded dollars in Seoul.
